reason: #2469: POSTERIOR_MEAN_VARIANCE_TOL and POSTERIOR_MEAN_CROSS_TOL (both 1e-10) decided when projected_bivariate_posterior_mean_result dropped a direction of the two-predictor posterior covariance. They were absolute variances in the predictors' own units, so the decision changed with the predictors' scale and not with anything the arithmetic could resolve. The decision is now the quadrature's own. The 2-D rule runs exactly when its zero-jitter Cholesky pivots, a and b - (c/sqrt(a))^2, formed with the same operations as cholesky_static, are both positive. Any other covariance is rank one in floating point, or indefinite. The nearest positive semidefinite covariance keeps only its major eigenpair, m + r with m = (a+b)/2 and r = hypot((a-b)/2, c), and the 1-D rule integrates along the major eigenvector. No positive eigenvalue means a point mass. A non-finite covariance is now refused. Before, f64::max turned a NaN variance into 0, and a NaN cross term made every Cholesky retry fail, so the helper silently returned the integrand at the mean.
evidence: git grep at 3e5348c94 finds both constants only in crates/gam-predict/src/lib.rs: the declarations at :555-556 and the three branches of projected_bivariate_posterior_mean_result at :798, :801 and :809. No test names either one. The helper's only callers are binomial_location_scale.rs:282, dispersion_location_scale.rs:139 and survival.rs:317, and each passes a symmetric covariance with diagonals already clamped at zero. normal_expectation_2d_adaptive_result reaches ghq_nd_integrate_try (gam-solve quadrature.rs:4319). That function clamps only negative diagonals, then factors through cholesky_static (:4262), which forms l00 = sqrt(cov[0][0]) and l10 = cov[1][0]/l00 and refuses when cov[1][1] - l10*l10 <= 0. The new predicate is those same operations, so every 2-D call now factors at retry 0 and never reaches the jitter ladder. For a = 0, c = 0 and b > 0 the major eigenvector is (0, 1) with variance b, so the 1-D nodes are the same as the old branch's. Not compiled or run locally (user directive); compile is covered by the lead's shared tip check.

reason: #2469: SEED_FEASIBILITY_TOL (1e-9) was a picked tolerance, declared twice as a function-local const, for certifying the strict-interior seed. The dense site allowed -1e-9 on equality-pair rows and 0.5*margin - 1e-9 on one-sided rows; the operator site allowed 0.5*ACTIVE_SET_INTERIOR_SEED_MARGIN - 1e-9. The QP that produces the seed guarantees a scaled violation of at most ACTIVE_SET_PRIMAL_FEASIBILITY_TOL on the margin-shifted rows (the contract documented on solve_strictly_convex_quadratic_with_constraint_set_dual). Both certificates now check exactly what that contract implies: slack >= margin - ACTIVE_SET_PRIMAL_FEASIBILITY_TOL on shifted rows and slack >= -ACTIVE_SET_PRIMAL_FEASIBILITY_TOL on unshifted equality-pair rows. That removes both the picked 1e-9 and the picked factor 0.5.

reason: #2469. The dispersion location-scale warm start seeded each row's log precision through dispersion_moment_log_precision_seed. It floored the seeded mean at 1e-12, the squared residual at 1e-8·μ² (1e-8·μ^p for Tweedie), the precision ratio at 1e-6 and the NB excess at its sampling resolution, then boxed the result to [LOG_PRECISION_FLOOR, LOG_PRECISION_CEILING] = [-10, 10]. The seed is now Smyth's double-GLM log-link working response at the pooled dispersion, which is linear in the per-row moment, so no row needs a floor and no box is needed, and a pooled moment with no finite seed is refused. The helper and its two function-local constants have no other caller.

The item list applies source_removal_guard.py's ITEM regex and occurrence rule by hand. Compile is covered by the lead's shared tip check.

reason: #2469: MIN_EPS = 1e-12 was an absolute floor on the Sinkhorn barycenter's entropic regularization. The barycenter of (c*cost, c*eps) is the same for every c > 0, so an absolute floor refused some scalings of a problem and accepted others. It also did not bound what its doc claimed. At unit cost and eps = 1e-12 the exponents carry about 12 fractional bits, but a cost of 1e4 at the same eps puts them past 2^53 and they resolve nothing. validate_inputs now refuses eps that is not finite and positive, and eps where the largest Gibbs exponent max(cost)/eps rounds by a nat or more (UNIT_ROUNDOFF*max(cost)/eps >= 1). sentinel_saturated_log_a_returns_error drove log_a to the sentinel with cost 1e288 at eps = MIN_EPS. Under the new bound every accepted exponent is above -2^53, so that input is refused before any update runs, and no accepted input reaches the saturation branch that test exercised. It is replaced by same_barycenter_at_any_cost_scale, and rejects_small_eps now pins the refusal at the resolution bound.

reason: SPEC rule 23 (#2469). refine_certified_start stopped once the pending Newton step fell to NEWTON_REFINE_CONVERGED_EPS·(1 + ‖t‖), a picked ratio of 1e-12 plus an absolute unit. The certificate in hand already fixes the stopping rule. From a certified iterate (h_k ≤ ½), the exact next step obeys η_{k+1} ≤ β_{k+1}·(L/2)·η_k², with β_{k+1} ≤ β_k/(1 − h_k) by the Banach perturbation lemma, so η_{k+1} ≤ h_k/(2(1 − h_k))·η_k. A computed step that fails that contraction is round-off in the field rather than Newton progress, and refinement stops at that iterate. An exactly zero step stops at once. Nothing is left for the constant to scale.
